comment: Dialogue. Story Bible: Dot Okafor, chief engineer. Eight coffee mugs, genius, chaotic. Worked under Dad.
notes: Code generated with AI assistance (Claude). Reviewed by team. What Dot says when the player talks to her in the Design Bay. Her lines turn the RocketEvaluator report into speech: one line per check, picked at random from the list for that check's result. Placeholders (filled from the report): {twr} liftoff thrust-to-weight; {margin} static margin in calibres; {when} 'on the pad' or 'once the fuel's gone'; {pct} range as % of what the trip needs; {short} % of the needed speed missing; {spare} % to spare; {q} max-Q kPa; {limit} structure limit kPa; {load} % of the limit; {stage} upper-stage number; {upper_twr} its thrust-to-weight; {cost} rocket cost $M; {budget} budget $M; {mug} a mug number 1-8. Stability uses the worse of liftoff/burnout; 'warn_wobbly' is a margin below 1 calibre, 'warn_stiff' above 3.
speaker: DOT
greeting: Ah. You've brought me a rocket. Hold on, let me find a mug that isn't cold. ...Mug {mug}. Right.
Show me what you've got. And mind the mugs, they're load-bearing.
Let's have a look at her. Don't tell me the numbers, I like to guess first.
Your dad used to stand exactly there and wait for me to say something nice. Let's see if I can.
no_rocket: That's a workbench with nothing on it. I can't check nothing. Well, I can. It passes.

pass: Thrust-to-weight of {twr}. She'll jump off the pad. Good.
{twr} times her own weight in push. That's a rocket that wants to leave.
warn: Liftoff's {twr}. She'll go up the way I get out of bed: slowly, and wasting a lot of energy.
{twr} to one. She'll lift, but she'll spend half her fuel just arguing with gravity.
fail: Thrust-to-weight {twr}. That's not a launch, that's a very loud sit-down. More engine or less rocket.
She's heavier than her engines can push. {twr}. Under one means she stays exactly where she is.

pass: Static margin {margin} calibres {when}. She'll fly straight as an arrow. Fins are doing their job.
{margin} calibres. Centre of pressure nicely behind the centre of mass. That's how you keep the pointy end in front.
warn_wobbly: Margin's only {margin} calibres {when}. She'll wobble like mug {mug} on a Friday. Bigger fins, or move the weight up.
{margin} calibres {when}. Close to the line. I'd want a bit more fin back there.
warn_stiff: {margin} calibres {when}. Too steady, if you can believe it. She'll weathervane into every gust. Trim those fins.
That's a weathervane, not a rocket. {margin} calibres. Smaller fins, she'll thank you.
fail: Margin {margin} calibres {when}. Negative-ish means she flips. Tail first. Every time. Bigger fins.
{margin} calibres {when}. Centre of pressure's ahead of the weight. She'll tumble before she clears the tower.

pass: Range is {pct}% of what the trip needs. {spare}% spare. Your dad would call that 'barely enough'. I call it plenty.
{pct}% of the delta-v we need. She gets there with fuel to spare. Lovely.
warn: {pct}% of what we need. She'll make it if nothing goes wrong. Something always goes wrong.
Just over the line at {pct}%. Margins. Leave more than you think you need.
fail: She runs dry at {pct}% of the speed we need. About {short}% short. More fuel, better engine, or lose some weight.
{pct}%. She'll go up, she'll come down, she won't stay up. Orbit's a speed, not a height.

pass: Max-Q about {q} kPa against a limit of {limit}. The skin holds. Good.
Air pushes {load}% as hard as she can take. She's tough enough.
warn: Max-Q {q} kPa, limit {limit}. That's {load}%. She'll hold, but I'll be holding my breath.
{load}% of her limit at max-Q. One gust and I'm on mug {mug}.
fail: Max-Q {q} kPa. Limit's {limit}. She folds up like a paper cup. Stronger skin, or don't go so fast so low.
{load}% of what the structure can take. That's not a rocket, that's confetti.

pass: Stage {stage} pushes at {upper_twr}. Enough to keep her climbing.
Stage {stage}'s fine. {upper_twr} to one up there where it counts.
warn: Stage {stage} only gets {upper_twr}. She'll sag back toward Earth while it builds speed. Heavier engine, or a lighter stage.
Stage {stage} at {upper_twr}. Weak little thing. It'll get there, eventually, maybe.

pass: Escape tower's on. If it goes wrong, they come home. That's the bit that matters.
warn: People on board and no escape tower. No. Coming back is harder than going up. Don't save weight on what keeps someone alive.

over: Lovely rocket. Costs ${cost}M. Pike gave us ${budget}M. I'm not the one telling him.
ok: And she's ${cost}M of Pike's ${budget}M. He'll still grumble.

3: Not one thing I'd change. ...Don't tell anyone I said that.
That's a good rocket. Your dad would have stood there grinning like an idiot. So go on. Grin.
2: One thing to fix and she's perfect. Or fly her as she is. Your call.
Nearly there. One warning. Fix it if you've got the money.
1: She'll fly. She'll complain the whole way, but she'll fly.
A few warnings. Nothing that kills her. Everything that annoys me.
0: Not yet. Fix the red ones. Take your time. Coffee helps. I'm told.
She won't make it like this. That's what the bench is for. Try again.
